findings.sentence: Overexpression of SIRT2 or treatment of mice with the NAD(+) precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) increases BubR1 abundance in vivo.
findings.caveats: NMN raised BubR1 in normal mice, not shown to rescue BubR1 H/H phenotypes; NMN is a supplement, not an approved drug; the nonsense allele of the child cannot be rescued, only protein from the missense allele might be stabilised.

findings.consequence: SIRT2 overexpression extends lifespan in BubR1 hypomorph
findings.system: BubR1 H/H mice, genetic SIRT2 transgene, 2014
findings.sentence: Overexpression of SIRT2 in BubR1(H/H) animals increases median lifespan, with a greater effect in male mice.
findings.caveats: Genetic overexpression, not a drug; sex-dependent; H/H is a low-wild-type-protein model, differs from nonsense plus missense compound heterozygote; lifespan only, not growth or tumours.

findings.consequence: clearance of p16+ senescent cells delays progeroid phenotypes
findings.sentence: In tissues--such as adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye--in which p16(Ink4a) contributes to the acquisition of age-related pathologies, life-long removal of p16(Ink4a)-expressing cells delayed onset of these phenotypes.
findings.caveats: Transgenic suicide system activated by AP20187 (not an approved drug); not a senolytic drug test; relevant to muscle atrophy in the child.

findings.consequence: late-life senescent cell clearance attenuates established disorders
findings.sentence: Furthermore, late-life clearance attenuated progression of already established age-related disorders.
findings.caveats: Same transgene; AP20187 not approved; senolytic drugs (dasatinib/quercetin, navitoclax) not tested in BubR1 models in retrieved literature.

findings.consequence: p16Ink4a inactivation attenuates senescence and ageing
findings.sentence: Inactivation of p16(Ink4a) in BubR1-insufficient mice attenuates both cellular senescence and premature ageing in these tissues.
findings.caveats: Genetic; p16 loss is tumour-permissive, risky in a cancer-prone child; tissues were muscle and fat.

findings.consequence: Pak2 depletion attenuates aging phenotypes and extends lifespan
findings.sentence: Importantly, depletion of Pak2 in BubR1 progeroid mice attenuated the onset of aging-associated phenotypes and extended life span.
findings.caveats: Genetic depletion; Pak2 inhibitors not tested; no approved Pak2 drug.

findings.consequence: sFRP3 inhibition restores body and brain size
findings.sentence: Using BubR1H/H mice as a novel mouse model of accelerated aging, we report that genetic inhibition of sFRP3 restores the reduced body and brain size observed in BubR1H/H mice.
findings.caveats: Genetic knockout, no drug; brain and neurogenesis focus.

findings.consequence: chromosome 15 transfer restores BubR1 and checkpoint response
findings.sentence: Microcell-mediated transfer of chromosome 15 (containing BUB1B) into the cells restored normal BubR1 levels, kinetochore localization of p55cdc, and the normal responses to colcemid treatment.
findings.caveats: Gene complementation proof of causality, not a drug; patients had monoallelic BUB1B mutations plus a decreased second allele.

findings.consequence: ROS scavengers, mitochondrial chaperones, apoptosis inhibition dampen aneuploidy effect on brain size
findings.sentence: We identify overexpression of Radical Oxygen Species scavengers, mitochondria chaperones and apoptosis inhibition as genetic interventions capable of dampening the deleterious effects of aneuploidy on brain size.
findings.caveats: Fly neural stem cell model, genetic interventions only; microcephaly not in this child.

findings.consequence: nicotinamide rescues CIN cell phenotypes (NAD+/ATP depletion)
findings.sentence: PARP activation causes depletion of its substrate, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) and subsequent loss of Adenosine Tri-Phosphate (ATP), and we found that adding ATP or nicotinamide (a precursor in the synthesis of NAD+) could rescue the observed phenotypes.
findings.caveats: Fly CIN cells under nucleotide-synthesis block, not BubR1 specifically; nicotinamide is vitamin B3 (approved status as a drug is low confidence), no dose data.

findings.consequence: HSCT with treosulfan RIC: haematologic recovery then graft rejection
findings.sentence: In conclusion, we demonstrate that RIC HSCT with TCRαβ+/CD19+ depletion was well tolerated and resulted in complete hematologic recovery in our MVA1 patient, but, unfortunately, it was followed by rapid graft rejection.
findings.caveats: Single patient with MDS/monosomy 7, died day +156; treosulfan used for HSCT conditioning; not generalisable to this child.

findings.consequence: bilateral nephrectomy without further chemotherapy: long remission
findings.system: PCS/MVA BUB1B child with bilateral Wilms tumour, case report, 2019
findings.sentence: The patient survived for 15 months after bilateral nephrectomy without peritoneal relapse, metastasis of Wilms tumor, or the occurrence of rhabdomyosarcoma and maintained a good quality of life while receiving peritoneal dialysis at home.
findings.caveats: Surgery, not a drug; Wilms not rhabdomyosarcoma; 15 months follow-up only.

findings.sentence: Finally, UPCP significantly inhibited HGPS cellular senescence and ameliorated progeroid phenotypes, extending the lifespan of LmnaG609G/G609G mice.
findings.caveats: Progerin-specific peptide; works through BUBR1 stabilisation in HGPS, not relevant to BUB1B variants.

background_evidence.consequence: cardiac BubR1 deficiency; sustaining expression proposed

background_evidence.sentence: Overall, our data suggest that BubR1 deficiency is a feature of cardiac aging and disease in humans, and that sustaining BubR1 expression may offer a potential therapeutic strategy to mitigate age-associated cardiac decline and improve heart health in the elderly.

no_evidence: No drug (approved or otherwise) tested in BubR1 H/H, H/L1002P or +/GTTA mice with phenotype rescue found; only genetic (SIRT2, p16, Pak2, sFRP3) or NMN-biomarker data.
No rapamycin, metformin or NAD+ precursor trial in BubR1-hypomorphic mouse phenotypes found in Europe PMC.
No senolytic drug (dasatinib, quercetin, navitoclax, fisetin) tested in a BubR1 model; only the INK-ATTAC transgene with AP20187.
No zebrafish, C. elegans or yeast BubR1/Mad3 intervention study found.
No iPSC, organoid or lymphoblast drug study of BUB1B/MVA patient cells found.
No drug screen on BUB1B patient fibroblasts found; only colcemid response and chromosome 15 complementation.
No nicotinamide riboside study in BubR1 models found.

note: Round-2 drug-agnostic search via Europe PMC REST (abstracts only; all source_section=abstract, verified=false, sentences copied from Europe PMC abstract text and re-checked by substring). The BubR1-model literature contains genetic rescues (SIRT2, p16 loss, Pak2, sFRP3, senescent-cell clearance) but no approved drug that rescues a BubR1-deficient phenotype; strongest L2 are genetic. L3 evidence is limited to case reports (treosulfan HSCT with graft rejection, dactinomycin intolerance, surgery). PMID 31184400 (RMS PCS-MVA reduced-intensity chemotherapy) had no abstract available and was not used. Risk signals: aneuploid-selective agents, p53/Arf inhibition, fasting, spindle-poison insensitivity. NMN is a supplement; nicotinamide marked approved=true with low confidence.
